# Pi Development — Map & Rules

## Golden rule: keep the fork at upstream shape

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter**; do **not** patch `pi-mono-fork` core (minimizes upstream drift / merge conflicts).

- Override core via hooks/filters (`pi.hooks.removeAction`, `pi.registerTool`, prompt/tool filters); wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields (pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`).
- No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is upstream surface area), never an inline one-off patch. Reverting a core patch → extension override is always preferred.
- Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge / cache-health / routine launch agents | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist`, `com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist`, `com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |
| Extension API reference / best practices | `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` |
| Setup registry (catalog YAML = source; `generated/` scanner-owned, never hand-edit) | `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` |
| Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?") | `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**: (1) make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials; (2) coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases; smoke-test every accepted shape. Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Gate: `node extensions/cache-base-prompt/test.mjs`. This is the lever for project/directory-specific caching.
- **`setActiveTools` is NOT idempotent** (fork `agent-harness.ts:941` always emits `tools_update` + a session write, even for an unchanged set — the documented "builtins removed ~2,560×/18d" burst source). An extension calling it per-turn from `before_agent_start` must guard: `if (sameNames(pi.getActiveTools(), desired)) return;` before the call, or it bursts the within-session `tools[]` cache. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.
- Verification gate after any extension/harness/skill change: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

|---|---|

| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**: (1) make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials; (2) coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases; smoke-test every accepted shape. Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Gate: `node extensions/cache-base-prompt/test.mjs`. This is the lever for project/directory-specific caching.
- **`setActiveTools` is NOT idempotent** (fork `agent-harness.ts:941` always emits `tools_update` + a session write, even for an unchanged set — the documented "builtins removed ~2,560×/18d" burst source). An extension calling it per-turn from `before_agent_start` must guard: `if (sameNames(pi.getActiveTools(), desired)) return;` before the call, or it bursts the within-session `tools[]` cache. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.
- Verification gate after any extension/harness/skill change: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

Dream upserts individual H2 sections when relevant events accumulate. Manual updates are fine; keep the file under ~5.8 kB to stay within the token budget. Regenerate the Active Projects section when the project mix shifts significantly.

## pi-memory — CC `extractMemories` parity (2026-05-30)

Write side is now per-turn extraction matching Claude Code's `extractMemories` (the 2026-05-16 "trigger gating" rev wrongly put `autoDream`'s 24h/5-session cadence on the *extraction* path — reverted). See `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md` and `docs/memory-architecture.md`. **Extraction fires at `turn_end`, per-turn**, throttled by `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS` (default 1 = CC every-turn), bounded by `maxTurns: 5` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_TURNS`) + `maxOutputTokens` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, default 2048). **No time/session gate on extraction** — the 24h/N-session consolidation cadence belongs to dream-memory (CC `autoDream`). Removed: `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS`, `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS`, `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS`, the `detectPriorityBump`/`force` path, `PI_MEMORY_TURN_END_TRIGGER`. Kept as deliberate deviations from literal CC: lock as a pure **write mutex** (`~/.pi/agent/memory/.consolidate-lock-<scope>`, PID body, mtime no longer state) guarding `MEMORY.md` against concurrent same-scope forks, and **pollution skip** (`web_search`/`mcp_*`/`WebFetch` etc. disqualify the session; threshold `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_THRESHOLD`, default 1). Shutdown flush still runs as a final extraction. `maxTurns` is a new fork-core agent-loop primitive (see `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`). Active-recall default OFF; opt-in via `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1`. Freshness caveats (≥1 day) wrap stale memories before injection.

## Pi Change Workflow

Use this before modifying `my-pi` or `pi-mono-fork`:

1. Read the local Pi docs above for the touched surface.
2. Choose extension/package first; write a short note if core changes are unavoidable.
3. Run Matt Pocock's architecture review lens: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/matt-pocock/references/improve-codebase-architecture.md`.
4. Make one incremental simplification when it is local, safe, and directly adjacent to the change.
5. Update `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` and governed docs for setup/runtime changes; never hand-edit `docs/pi-setup/generated/`.

## Cache Stability (mandatory for fork + extension work)

Any change touching `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors **must** review the `pi-cache-stability` skill first. Anthropic prompt cache only helps when the prefix is byte-identical and alive within TTL — pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. The skill captures the L1/L2/L3 levers (`context: "slim"|"none"`, `systemPrompt` override, `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h`), the audit checklist, and the verification recipe. Source-of-truth doc: `docs/cache-strategy.md`.

## Pre-PR local review

Before opening, updating, or declaring a PR ready, run a local review pass against the diff.

Review lenses:

- Extension/package-first: custom behavior belongs in `my-pi` extensions or pi packages unless the PR proves core is required.
- Local Pi docs: PRs that touch extension/package/SDK/core surfaces cite the relevant file under `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/`.
- Matt Pocock architecture lens: run the `improve-codebase-architecture` reference and record any accepted/deferred deepening opportunity.
- `instruction-refiner`: prompt, AGENTS.md, skill, tool, and other model-facing instruction changes.
- `code-craft`: non-trivial code, public API shape, names, reader flow, data movement, module boundaries, and needless abstraction.
- Dedup / lean-down: repeated extension glue, scripts, prompts, package metadata, docs, helpers, or package boundaries.
- Docs / evals: behavior, runtime, setup, prompt/context, or recall changes need matching docs and tests/evals.
- `agent-ci`: run local GitHub Actions CI and fix failures before handoff.

Use:

```bash
npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure
```

If paused, fix the issue and retry with the emitted `retry` command. Do not report work as done until agent-ci passes or a real blocker is named.

Stop before PR if review finds a real P1. Fix it or document why it is intentionally deferred.

## Review guidelines

- Flag P1 when custom functionality lands in `pi-mono-fork` core without evidence that extension/package APIs cannot support it.
- Flag P1 when a Pi setup/runtime change skips catalog YAML, governed docs, or the architecture review lens.
- Flag P1 when model-facing instructions add vague guidance, duplicate rules, stale links, or long rationale that should be compressed or moved to a focused doc.
- Flag P1 when code obscures the reader flow: vague names, hidden data movement, needless abstraction, grab-bag helpers, or public APIs that make the simple path complex.
- Flag P1 when extensions, scripts, docs, package metadata, or prompts duplicate the same concept and should share one package, helper, or documented source of truth.
- Flag P1 when prompt/context changes can affect recall, tool routing, cache stability, or session startup cost without matching tests/evals/docs.
- Flag P1 when runtime/setup changes skip `docs/pi-setup/` catalog updates, governed docs, or relevant runbooks.
- Treat docs typos, broken links, and stale command examples as P1 when they affect agent behavior or setup safety.
- Prefer follow-up notes over findings for speculative extraction; require concrete repeated use or a clear package boundary before recommending shared packages.

## Verification

Before changing runtime extension behavior, run the relevant eval or add one if none exists.

- When installing, adding, modifying, or removing Pi extensions/packages, run the my-pi extension checks and the fork cache gate together:
  - `npm run test:extension-gate`
    - Includes profile cache contracts, prompt-health fixtures, claude-bridge cache markers, dream-memory cache tests, skill/tool search, native aliases, Agent view, and task tools.

  - `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- Treat a failing `pi-mono-fork` build/cache gate as a blocker for extension rollout; extensions must pass against the fork they ship with.

content.text:
**Verdaccio** is a tiny self-hosted npm registry/proxy. "On `lue-kube`" = run it as a pod in your personal Kubernetes cluster. It sits in front of your packages and **caches** them in-cluster.

What it buys you over GH Packages alone:
- **In-cluster cache/proxy** — pods/runners pull from Verdaccio (inside the cluster), which caches `@valkyriweb/*` *and* public deps. No GitHub egress per build, no PAT distributed to every pod, no GH rate limits.
- **Offline resilience** — if GitHub is unreachable (outage, or a pod with no outbound internet / locked-down NetworkPolicy), the in-cluster cache still serves the last-good versions. Builds don't break because github.com hiccuped.
- **One endpoint** — every k8s pod / action runner / clawsweeper points at one in-cluster URL instead of juggling GH auth.

The cost: it's another service to run — Deployment + PVC (stores cached tarballs) + Service, auth config, uplink config. Real maintenance surface.

**My take: confirmed GH Packages `@valkyriweb` as primary/source-of-truth. Defer Verdaccio** — don't build it up front, it's YAGNI until a concrete trigger hits:
- a pod runtime that genuinely can't reach github.com, **or**
- GH Packages egress/auth/rate-limit pain once the fleet is actually pulling a lot, **or**
- you want builds to survive a GitHub outage.

Until one of those bites, GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. So: **good idea, wrong time** — keep it as the tracked fallback, stand it up on trigger.

The docs already frame it as the offline alt; let me make the "defer until trigger" decision explicit so a future session doesn't build it prematurely:

# Release Engineering

read_when: setting up versioned builds; landing a change to any fork package or extension; debugging non-reproducible pod/clawsweeper images; wiring cache/prompt-stability gates into CI; rolling back a runtime to a known-good version.

---

## Problem: file: links are not a release boundary

Every runtime currently resolves fork packages via `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies`:

```
"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core":   "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-ai":           "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/ai"
"@earendil-works/pi-tui":          "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/tui"
```

Consequence: `npm install` on a pod or action runner resolves to whatever the filesystem has at build time. Two builds from the same commit can produce different binaries if the fork checkout differs. Rollback is "re-checkout the fork at some commit and rebuild" — fragile, undocumented, invisible.

The fix is a **versioned registry seam**: publish fork packages and extension/profile packages to a scoped registry; each runtime pins a profile version; rollback = redeploy the previous tag.

---

## Registry

**Primary**: GitHub Packages, scope `@valkyriweb`.
- Auth: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` = GitHub PAT with `packages:write`. Already available in the `valkyriweb` org.
- Registry URL: `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
- `.npmrc` in fork root and `my-pi` root: `@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`

**Alternate for offline pods**: Verdaccio on `lue-kube` (self-hosted). Mirror `@valkyriweb` scope from GitHub Packages. Use this when a pod runtime has no outbound internet to GitHub.

During development (laptop only): `file:` links remain in place. Kill file: links only for release builds — see "Kill file: links" below.

---

## Three release layers

### Layer 1 — Fork packages (upstream baseline + platform delta)

Packages: `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent`, `@valkyriweb/pi-agent-core`, `@valkyriweb/pi-ai`, `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`.

These are the `@earendil-works/*` fork packages republished under the `@valkyriweb` scope with a SemVer version that encodes the upstream baseline + the platform-delta commits on top.

Version scheme: `<upstream-version>-luke.<N>` e.g. `0.78.0-luke.3`. Patch bump on each fork-delta release. Major/minor track upstream.

Add `publishConfig` to each fork `package.json`:
```json
"publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }
```

### Layer 2 — Extensions + profile manifests

Each extension under `my-pi/extensions/` and each profile manifest under `my-pi/packages/` becomes its own versioned package with a `peerDependency` on the Layer 1 fork range:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
}
```

Published as e.g. `@valkyriweb/pi-ext-native-tool-overrides`, `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full`.

A profile manifest `package.json` declares `dependencies` on the exact extension versions it bundles — this is the "what runs here" bill of materials.

### Layer 3 — Per-runtime lockfile pin

Each runtime (laptop, openclaw, pod, clawsweeper) pins a single profile version in its `package.json` or deployment manifest:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/my-pi-full": "1.4.2"
}
```

`npm ci` against the lockfile produces a reproducible image. "What runs here" is one version number.

Pod/clawsweeper: build image with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, bake into the container image layer. Rollback = redeploy the container image tagged at the previous profile version.

---

## Tooling: Changesets

Use `@changesets/cli` for the release flow. Do not hand-bump versions.

Workflow:
1. Every PR that changes a fork package or extension includes a `changeset` file (`npx changeset add`). The changeset declares which packages changed and the semver impact (patch/minor/major).
2. On merge to `main`, the "Version Packages" PR is opened automatically by the Changesets GitHub Action. This PR bumps versions and updates `CHANGELOG.md` for each affected package.
3. Merging the Version Packages PR triggers the publish step: `npm run build && npx changeset publish`.
4. Tags are pushed atomically with the publish. Rollback = redeploy the tag.

Config: `.changeset/config.json` in both `pi-mono-fork` and `my-pi` roots.

---

## Kill file: links for release

The `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies` are for local dev. For release builds, swap them for the versioned `@valkyriweb` references.

Pattern: maintain a `scripts/release-deps.mjs` that rewrites `package.json` `devDependencies` in place before `npm publish`, restoring them after. Or maintain a separate `package.release.json` that the CI build uses.

Do NOT commit the rewritten `package.json` to `main`. The `file:` links stay for the laptop dev loop.

---

## Per-runtime lockfile pinning + reproducible builds

- Runtimes: laptop (`my-pi-full`), openclaw (`my-pi-harness`), k8s pods (`my-pi-pod`), action runners / clawsweeper.
- Each runtime directory contains a committed `package-lock.json` generated from pinned Layer 3 deps.
- Builds run `npm ci` (not `npm install`) — this reads the lockfile exactly, fails if it is out of date.
- Pod image Dockerfile: `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` then `RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`.
- Tag rollback: `docker pull ghcr.io/valkyriweb/my-pi-pod:<previous-tag>` + redeploy. No rebuild required.

---

## CI: PR gate vs release gate

### PR gate (runs on every pull_request to main in both repos)

**Current fork CI** (`pi-mono-fork/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `fork-safety-check`): `npm ci --ignore-scripts` → `npm run build` → `npm run check` (fork canonical check) → `./pi-test.sh --no-env --version` (CLI smoke). It does **not** yet run `test:build-gate`. The `test:build-gate` script exists (it chains the build + cache/prompt sub-tests) but wiring it into fork CI is **WS-E scope** — see Release gate below.

`my-pi` has no CI yet. Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:extension-gate
      - run: npm run check:profiles
```

### Release gate (runs before Changesets publish, blocks on failure)

Add a `release-gate` job in the Changesets publish workflow:
```yaml
jobs:
  release-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm run test:extension-gate                       # my-pi: cache + prompt-health + profile gates
      - run: npm --prefix ../pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate  # fork: build + cache/prompt sub-tests
  publish:
    needs: release-gate   # publish only if gate passes
    ...
```

**Cache and prompt stability tests are BLOCKING release acceptance.** A red stability test blocks the publish — the tag is never created, the registry is never written.

### Required status checks

Ensure these are listed as required in GitHub repo branch protection settings:
- `pi-mono-fork/main`: `fork-safety-check` (the `ci.yml` job)
- `my-pi/main`: `gate` (once the workflow above is added)

---

## Open gaps (pre-release state)

| Gap | Action needed |
|---|---|
| No `publishConfig` in fork packages | Add to each `pi-mono-fork/packages/*/package.json` |
| No Changesets config | `npx changeset init` in both repos |
| No `my-pi` CI workflow | Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as above |
| `test:prompt-health:live` requires running pi | Exclude from CI or add fixture/offline mode |
| `test:cache-diagnostics` not in `test:extension-gate` | Wire it in if it asserts Codex-side cache invariants |
| Branch protection on `pi-mono-fork` unconfirmed | Verify `fork-safety-check` is a required status check at Settings → Branches → main |
| Verdaccio on `lue-kube` not provisioned | Track in `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` when stood up |

---

## Related docs

- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — what the fork carries and why
- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md` — rebase + cherry-pick workflow
- `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — cache stability source of truth
- `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` — runtime fleet map
- `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` — L1-L4 config model (extensionConfig seam)

Until then GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. When stood up, track in `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.

# Release Engineering

read_when: setting up versioned builds; landing a change to any fork package or extension; debugging non-reproducible pod/clawsweeper images; wiring cache/prompt-stability gates into CI; rolling back a runtime to a known-good version.

---

## Problem: file: links are not a release boundary

Every runtime currently resolves fork packages via `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies`:

```
"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core":   "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-ai":           "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/ai"
"@earendil-works/pi-tui":          "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/tui"
```

Consequence: `npm install` on a pod or action runner resolves to whatever the filesystem has at build time. Two builds from the same commit can produce different binaries if the fork checkout differs. Rollback is "re-checkout the fork at some commit and rebuild" — fragile, undocumented, invisible.

The fix is a **versioned registry seam**: publish fork packages and extension/profile packages to a scoped registry; each runtime pins a profile version; rollback = redeploy the previous tag.

---

## Registry

**Primary**: GitHub Packages, scope `@valkyriweb`.
- Auth: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` = GitHub PAT with `packages:write`. Already available in the `valkyriweb` org.
- Registry URL: `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
- `.npmrc` in fork root and `my-pi` root: `@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`

**Alternate for offline pods**: Verdaccio on `lue-kube` (self-hosted in-cluster registry/proxy that caches `@valkyriweb/*` + public deps). **Decision (2026-05-30): GitHub Packages is primary/source-of-truth; Verdaccio is deferred** — do NOT stand it up until a concrete trigger: (a) a pod/runtime that genuinely cannot reach github.com, (b) GH Packages egress/auth/rate-limit pain once the fleet pulls heavily, or (c) builds must survive a GitHub outage. Until then GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. When stood up, track in `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.

During development (laptop only): `file:` links remain in place. Kill file: links only for release builds — see "Kill file: links" below.

---

## Three release layers

### Layer 1 — Fork packages (upstream baseline + platform delta)

Packages: `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent`, `@valkyriweb/pi-agent-core`, `@valkyriweb/pi-ai`, `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`.

These are the `@earendil-works/*` fork packages republished under the `@valkyriweb` scope with a SemVer version that encodes the upstream baseline + the platform-delta commits on top.

Version scheme: `<upstream-version>-luke.<N>` e.g. `0.78.0-luke.3`. Patch bump on each fork-delta release. Major/minor track upstream.

Add `publishConfig` to each fork `package.json`:
```json
"publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }
```

### Layer 2 — Extensions + profile manifests

Each extension under `my-pi/extensions/` and each profile manifest under `my-pi/packages/` becomes its own versioned package with a `peerDependency` on the Layer 1 fork range:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
}
```

Published as e.g. `@valkyriweb/pi-ext-native-tool-overrides`, `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full`.

A profile manifest `package.json` declares `dependencies` on the exact extension versions it bundles — this is the "what runs here" bill of materials.

### Layer 3 — Per-runtime lockfile pin

Each runtime (laptop, openclaw, pod, clawsweeper) pins a single profile version in its `package.json` or deployment manifest:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/my-pi-full": "1.4.2"
}
```

`npm ci` against the lockfile produces a reproducible image. "What runs here" is one version number.

Pod/clawsweeper: build image with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, bake into the container image layer. Rollback = redeploy the container image tagged at the previous profile version.

---

## Tooling: Changesets

Use `@changesets/cli` for the release flow. Do not hand-bump versions.

Workflow:
1. Every PR that changes a fork package or extension includes a `changeset` file (`npx changeset add`). The changeset declares which packages changed and the semver impact (patch/minor/major).
2. On merge to `main`, the "Version Packages" PR is opened automatically by the Changesets GitHub Action. This PR bumps versions and updates `CHANGELOG.md` for each affected package.
3. Merging the Version Packages PR triggers the publish step: `npm run build && npx changeset publish`.
4. Tags are pushed atomically with the publish. Rollback = redeploy the tag.

Config: `.changeset/config.json` in both `pi-mono-fork` and `my-pi` roots.

---

## Kill file: links for release

The `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies` are for local dev. For release builds, swap them for the versioned `@valkyriweb` references.

Pattern: maintain a `scripts/release-deps.mjs` that rewrites `package.json` `devDependencies` in place before `npm publish`, restoring them after. Or maintain a separate `package.release.json` that the CI build uses.

Do NOT commit the rewritten `package.json` to `main`. The `file:` links stay for the laptop dev loop.

---

## Per-runtime lockfile pinning + reproducible builds

- Runtimes: laptop (`my-pi-full`), openclaw (`my-pi-harness`), k8s pods (`my-pi-pod`), action runners / clawsweeper.
- Each runtime directory contains a committed `package-lock.json` generated from pinned Layer 3 deps.
- Builds run `npm ci` (not `npm install`) — this reads the lockfile exactly, fails if it is out of date.
- Pod image Dockerfile: `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` then `RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev`.
- Tag rollback: `docker pull ghcr.io/valkyriweb/my-pi-pod:<previous-tag>` + redeploy. No rebuild required.

---

## CI: PR gate vs release gate

### PR gate (runs on every pull_request to main in both repos)

**Current fork CI** (`pi-mono-fork/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `fork-safety-check`): `npm ci --ignore-scripts` → `npm run build` → `npm run check` (fork canonical check) → `./pi-test.sh --no-env --version` (CLI smoke). It does **not** yet run `test:build-gate`. The `test:build-gate` script exists (it chains the build + cache/prompt sub-tests) but wiring it into fork CI is **WS-E scope** — see Release gate below.

`my-pi` has no CI yet. Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:extension-gate
      - run: npm run check:profiles
```

### Release gate (runs before Changesets publish, blocks on failure)

Add a `release-gate` job in the Changesets publish workflow:
```yaml
jobs:
  release-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm run test:extension-gate                       # my-pi: cache + prompt-health + profile gates
      - run: npm --prefix ../pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate  # fork: build + cache/prompt sub-tests
  publish:
    needs: release-gate   # publish only if gate passes
    ...
```

**Cache and prompt stability tests are BLOCKING release acceptance.** A red stability test blocks the publish — the tag is never created, the registry is never written.

### Required status checks

Ensure these are listed as required in GitHub repo branch protection settings:
- `pi-mono-fork/main`: `fork-safety-check` (the `ci.yml` job)
- `my-pi/main`: `gate` (once the workflow above is added)

---

## Open gaps (pre-release state)

| Gap | Action needed |
|---|---|
| No `publishConfig` in fork packages | Add to each `pi-mono-fork/packages/*/package.json` |
| No Changesets config | `npx changeset init` in both repos |
| No `my-pi` CI workflow | Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as above |
| `test:prompt-health:live` requires running pi | Exclude from CI or add fixture/offline mode |
| `test:cache-diagnostics` not in `test:extension-gate` | Wire it in if it asserts Codex-side cache invariants |
| Branch protection on `pi-mono-fork` unconfirmed | Verify `fork-safety-check` is a required status check at Settings → Branches → main |
| Verdaccio on `lue-kube` not provisioned | Track in `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` when stood up |

---

## Related docs

- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — what the fork carries and why
- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md` — rebase + cherry-pick workflow
- `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — cache stability source of truth
- `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` — runtime fleet map
- `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` — L1-L4 config model (extensionConfig seam)

## pi-memory — CC `extractMemories` parity (2026-05-30)

Write side is now per-turn extraction matching Claude Code's `extractMemories` (the 2026-05-16 "trigger gating" rev wrongly put `autoDream`'s 24h/5-session cadence on the *extraction* path — reverted). See `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md` and `docs/memory-architecture.md`. **Extraction fires at `turn_end`, per-turn**, throttled by `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS` (default 1 = CC every-turn), bounded by `maxTurns: 5` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_TURNS`) + `maxOutputTokens` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, default 2048). **No time/session gate on extraction** — the 24h/N-session consolidation cadence belongs to dream-memory (CC `autoDream`). Removed: `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS`, `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS`, `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS`, the `detectPriorityBump`/`force` path, `PI_MEMORY_TURN_END_TRIGGER`. Kept as deliberate deviations from literal CC: lock as a pure **write mutex** (`~/.pi/agent/memory/.consolidate-lock-<scope>`, PID body, mtime no longer state) guarding `MEMORY.md` against concurrent same-scope forks, and **pollution skip** (`web_search`/`mcp_*`/`WebFetch` etc. disqualify the session; threshold `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_THRESHOLD`, default 1). Shutdown flush still runs as a final extraction. `maxTurns` is a new fork-core agent-loop primitive (see `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`). Active-recall default OFF; opt-in via `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1`. Freshness caveats (≥1 day) wrap stale memories before injection.

## Pi Change Workflow

Use this before modifying `my-pi` or `pi-mono-fork`:

1. Read the local Pi docs above for the touched surface.
2. Choose extension/package first; write a short note if core changes are unavoidable.
3. Run Matt Pocock's architecture review lens: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/matt-pocock/references/improve-codebase-architecture.md`.
4. Make one incremental simplification when it is local, safe, and directly adjacent to the change.
5. Update `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` and governed docs for setup/runtime changes; never hand-edit `docs/pi-setup/generated/`.

## Cache Stability (mandatory for fork + extension work)

Any change touching `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors **must** review the `pi-cache-stability` skill first. Anthropic prompt cache only helps when the prefix is byte-identical and alive within TTL — pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. The skill captures the L1/L2/L3 levers (`context: "slim"|"none"`, `systemPrompt` override, `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h`), the audit checklist, and the verification recipe. Source-of-truth doc: `docs/cache-strategy.md`.

## Pre-PR local review

Before opening, updating, or declaring a PR ready, run a local review pass against the diff.

Review lenses:

- Extension/package-first: custom behavior belongs in `my-pi` extensions or pi packages unless the PR proves core is required.
- Local Pi docs: PRs that touch extension/package/SDK/core surfaces cite the relevant file under `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/`.
- Matt Pocock architecture lens: run the `improve-codebase-architecture` reference and record any accepted/deferred deepening opportunity.
- `instruction-refiner`: prompt, AGENTS.md, skill, tool, and other model-facing instruction changes.
- `code-craft`: non-trivial code, public API shape, names, reader flow, data movement, module boundaries, and needless abstraction.
- Dedup / lean-down: repeated extension glue, scripts, prompts, package metadata, docs, helpers, or package boundaries.
- Docs / evals: behavior, runtime, setup, prompt/context, or recall changes need matching docs and tests/evals.
- `agent-ci`: run local GitHub Actions CI and fix failures before handoff.

Use:

```bash
npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure
```

If paused, fix the issue and retry with the emitted `retry` command. Do not report work as done until agent-ci passes or a real blocker is named.

Stop before PR if review finds a real P1. Fix it or document why it is intentionally deferred.

## Review guidelines

- Flag P1 when custom functionality lands in `pi-mono-fork` core without evidence that extension/package APIs cannot support it.
- Flag P1 when a Pi setup/runtime change skips catalog YAML, governed docs, or the architecture review lens.
- Flag P1 when model-facing instructions add vague guidance, duplicate rules, stale links, or long rationale that should be compressed or moved to a focused doc.
- Flag P1 when code obscures the reader flow: vague names, hidden data movement, needless abstraction, grab-bag helpers, or public APIs that make the simple path complex.
- Flag P1 when extensions, scripts, docs, package metadata, or prompts duplicate the same concept and should share one package, helper, or documented source of truth.
- Flag P1 when prompt/context changes can affect recall, tool routing, cache stability, or session startup cost without matching tests/evals/docs.
- Flag P1 when runtime/setup changes skip `docs/pi-setup/` catalog updates, governed docs, or relevant runbooks.
- Treat docs typos, broken links, and stale command examples as P1 when they affect agent behavior or setup safety.
- Prefer follow-up notes over findings for speculative extraction; require concrete repeated use or a clear package boundary before recommending shared packages.

# Pi Development — Map & Rules

## Golden rule: no behavior delta in core; route through the platform layer

The fork is ~228 commits ahead of upstream (`earendil-works/pi-mono`) — the goal is **not** to keep it at upstream shape, it is to keep every commit classifiable and the rebase surface shrinkable. Three tiers (grep-verified against upstream):

- **upstream-native** (zero maintenance): `pi.on(event,…)` event bus, `registerTool`, `registerFlag`/`getFlag`, `getActiveTools`/`setActiveTools`, `deepMergeSettings`, `<project_context>` block. Build freely.
- **platform delta** (good, generic, low rebase surface — these are *Luke's own* primitives, **not** upstream): the hooks/filters layer (`addFilter`/`applyFilters`/`removeAction`/`addAction`/`ExtensionHooksAPI`), the cache-split (`splitSystemPromptForCache`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY`), the `systemPrompt:build` filter, `<system-context>` carrier, agent subsystem, OTEL. They ride on top of the upstream `on()` bus. Write new platform primitives generically so they can be upstream-PR'd (each PR shrinks the rebase surface). Tag in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `… (platform)`.
- **behavior delta** (forbidden as inline core patches): any opinion about what pi *does* — prompts, tool logic, agent behavior, Luke-specific routing. Route via extension + hook/filter, never inline in `pi-mono-fork` core.

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter** (wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields — pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`). No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is rebase surface), never an inline behavior patch. Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. ## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**: (1) make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials; (2) coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases; smoke-test every accepted shape. Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Config layering

Four layers, precedence low → high. Deep detail: `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md`.

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | extension source defaults | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | including/excluding an extension |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}`, deep-merged global ← project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | env var / CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

- Keep defaults in extension-owned config files or typed source defaults; keep operator tuning in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json`; use env vars only as L4 overrides for one-off runs, secrets, CI, or emergency flips.
- New extension settings go in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json` — never new top-level `Settings` keys, never env-only configuration.
- `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor on `ExtensionAPI` is the missing ~15 LOC piece (`createExtensionAPI` has no settings handle yet — `loader.ts:254`); track as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed. Until it lands, extensions may read `settings.json` directly, then apply env overrides.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Gate: `node extensions/cache-base-prompt/test.mjs`. This is the lever for project/directory-specific caching.
- **`setActiveTools` is NOT idempotent** (fork `agent-harness.ts:941` always emits `tools_update` + a session write, even for an unchanged set — the documented "builtins removed ~2,560×/18d" burst source). An extension calling it per-turn from `before_agent_start` must guard: `if (sameNames(pi.getActiveTools(), desired)) return;` before the call, or it bursts the within-session `tools[]` cache. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.

# Config Layering

read_when: adding a new extension setting; migrating an env-var feature flag to settings.json; implementing getExtensionConfig; understanding why a setting override isn't taking effect; designing a new extension that needs per-project tuning.

---

## The L1-L4 model (precedence low → high)

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Who sets it | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | Extension source code (hardcoded defaults) | Extension author | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | Profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | `my-pi/packages/my-pi-*/package.json` | Including/excluding an extension from a profile |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}` block, deep-merged global ← project | Operator / Luke per-runtime or per-project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | Env var or CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | Shell environment, launch agent, CI secret | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

Higher layer wins. L4 always beats L3. L3 project settings beat L3 global settings (deep-merged, project keys win on conflict).

---

## Why this order

- **L1** is the extension's own defaults — it works with zero config.
- **L2** controls whether the extension loads at all. A miscategorized extension in the wrong profile is an L2 error.
- **L3** is the operator contract: `settings.json` is the stable, committed, reviewable place to tune behavior across runtimes. It survives restarts and is diffable.
- **L4** is the escape hatch: env vars and flags can override L3 without editing files — useful for CI secrets, one-off dev runs, emergency flips. They are not committed.

---

## extensionConfig{} in settings.json

Any `settings.json` (global at `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or project-local) may contain an `extensionConfig` key. The value is a plain object keyed by extension name (matching the extension's directory / package name). Values are arbitrary — whatever shape the extension expects.

```json
{
  "extensionConfig": {
    "cache-base-prompt": {
      "extendBase": true
    },
    "dream-memory": {
      "intervalMinutes": 30,
      "maxStoredItems": 200
    },
    "pi-memory": {
      "maxTurns": 5
    }
  }
}
```

Deep-merge behavior (from `deepMergeSettings` in `settings-manager.ts`): the global settings are the base; project settings are merged on top. For nested objects like `extensionConfig`, keys from the project object win at the leaf level — arrays are replaced, not concatenated.

This already works today. The settings JSON parser does NOT strip unknown keys (verified at `settings-manager.ts:334/408`), so `extensionConfig` blobs survive the parse and reach extensions unchanged.

---

## getExtensionConfig accessor (missing piece, ~15 LOC)

The only missing piece is a typed accessor on `ExtensionAPI` so extensions can read their config slice without reaching into the raw settings object.

Proposed signature (upstream-shaped, generic, ~15 LOC):

```typescript
// Method on the `api` object built by createExtensionAPI (loader.ts:254).
// NOTE: there is no settings handle in createExtensionAPI today — see caveat below.
getExtensionConfig<T = unknown>(namespace: string): T | undefined {
  return mergedSettings.extensionConfig?.[namespace] as T | undefined;
}
```

**Implementation caveat (verified):** `createExtensionAPI(extension, runtime, cwd, eventBus)` (`loader.ts:254`) does NOT receive the merged `Settings`, and neither it nor `ExtensionRuntime` exposes a `getSettings()`. So WS-B step 1 must first thread the merged settings (or a `() => Settings` getter) into the factory before the accessor can read anything. Do not assume an existing accessor.

Usage in an extension:

```typescript
pi.on("init", (pi) => {
  const cfg = pi.getExtensionConfig<{ extendBase?: boolean }>("cache-base-prompt");
  const extendBase = cfg?.extendBase ?? false;
  // ...
});
```

This is **upstreamable** — it is a generic, vendor-neutral accessor on the existing settings merge path. The `extensionConfig` key is just a convention namespace; upstream doesn't need to know what any extension puts in it.

Target: interface in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts`; implementation on the `api` object in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` (`createExtensionAPI`, `loader.ts:254`). Track in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed.

---

## Migration example: cache-base-prompt

**Current state (L4 only):**

```
# ~/.zshenv
export PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1
```

Extension reads:
```typescript
const extendBase = process.env.PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT === "1";
```

This works on the laptop where `~/.zshenv` is sourced. It is invisible on pod/harness runtimes that don't source that file.

**Target state (L3 primary, L4 override):**

1. Add to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (global, applies to all runtimes):
```json
{
  "extensionConfig": {
    "cache-base-prompt": { "extendBase": true }
  }
}
```

2. Update extension to read L3 first, fall back to L4:
```typescript
pi.on("init", (pi) => {
  const cfg = pi.getExtensionConfig<{ extendBase?: boolean }>("cache-base-prompt");
  const extendBase = cfg?.extendBase ?? (process.env.PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT === "1");
  // ...
});
```

3. Keep `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT` as L4 override — it still works, it just no longer needs to be set everywhere. Remove it from `~/.zshenv` once all runtimes have the `settings.json` entry.

This is the proof-of-concept for the whole model. Once `getExtensionConfig` lands, migrate other env-var flags the same way.

---

## Per-runtime settings.json locations

| Runtime | settings.json path |
|---|---|
| Laptop (full) | `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (global) + `<project>/.pi/settings.json` (project) |
| openclaw (harness) | agentDir configured in the harness launch — check `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| k8s pods (pod) | Mounted as a ConfigMap or baked into the image; see pod deployment manifest |
| Action runners / clawsweeper | Set via env or a mounted config file per the clawsweeper deployment |

Project-level settings override global for that project directory only. If you need a setting everywhere, put it in the global file.

---

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't read `process.env.*` directly in new extension code** without an L3 fallback. Env vars are invisible to other runtimes and not diffable.
- **Don't add top-level keys to `Settings`** for extension-specific config. Use `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` — it keeps the namespace clean and avoids upstream schema conflicts.
- **Don't rely on L2 (profile membership) to carry behavior defaults** — that conflates "does this extension load" with "how is it tuned". Load via L2, tune via L3.

---

## Related docs

- `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — cache + system-prompt stability (read before touching extensionConfig keys that affect prompt construction)
- `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` — extension authoring conventions
- `my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — versioned registry seam (how L3 settings reach each runtime at deploy time)
- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — track `getExtensionConfig` as a fork-first patch until upstreamed

6	
7	The fork (~228 commits ahead of `earendil-works/pi-mono`) is stable and feature-rich but has no versioned seam, no reproducible release, and no per-extension tuning surface. This program installs the missing platform infrastructure in five landable workstreams: a versioned registry (WS-A), a config-layering accessor (WS-B), typed Effect boundaries in extensions (WS-C), architectural review gates on every PR (WS-D), and blocking cache/prompt stability gates in release CI (WS-E). It also updates the docs/instructions so every future session starts with the full picture (WS-DOCS).
8	
9	**Golden-rule reframe — three tiers of change:**
10	
11	| Tier | Definition | Cost | Examples |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| **upstream-native** | Uses `pi.on`, `registerTool`, `registerFlag/getFlag`, `deepMergeSettings`, `<project_context>` — zero maintenance | free | any new extension using only the event bus |
14	| **platform delta** | Fork-only additive primitives: hooks/filters layer, `splitSystemPromptForCache`, `systemPrompt:build` filter, agent subsystem, OTEL | carries rebase surface; upstream-PR generics to shrink it | `getExtensionConfig` accessor (WS-B), new hooks added for WS-A |
15	| **behavior delta** | Inline patch to core behavior, not via hook/filter | forbidden; log in patch-inventory if unavoidable | — |
16	
17	Rule: route new customization through the platform layer. Upstream-PR each generic platform-delta primitive once it matures in the fork.
18	
19	## 4-layer config model
20	
21	| Layer | What it is | Mechanism | Precedence |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **L1 Capability** | Extension source code — built-in defaults | compiled constants / fallback values | lowest |
24	| **L2 Membership** | Profile manifest selects which extensions load | `pi.extensions[]` in profile `package.json` | ↑ |
25	| **L3 Tuning** | `settings.json extensionConfig{}` — per-extension key/value, deep-merged global ← project | `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor (WS-B) | ↑ |
26	| **L4 Override** | Env var / `--flag` for ephemeral or CI-level overrides | `registerFlag/getFlag`; env var fallback in accessor | highest |

# Goal: pi platform program — release engineering, config layering, Effect adoption, review gates

Created 2026-05-30T07:50:47Z. Multi-workstream; WS-B is the proof-of-concept first step; WS-A and WS-E are the release backbone. Work any WS independently; each has its own acceptance gate.

## Intent

The fork (~228 commits ahead of `earendil-works/pi-mono`) is stable and feature-rich but has no versioned seam, no reproducible release, and no per-extension tuning surface. This program installs the missing platform infrastructure in five landable workstreams: a versioned registry (WS-A), a config-layering accessor (WS-B), typed Effect boundaries in extensions (WS-C), architectural review gates on every PR (WS-D), and blocking cache/prompt stability gates in release CI (WS-E). It also updates the docs/instructions so every future session starts with the full picture (WS-DOCS).

**Golden-rule reframe — three tiers of change:**

| Tier | Definition | Cost | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **upstream-native** | Uses `pi.on`, `registerTool`, `registerFlag/getFlag`, `deepMergeSettings`, `<project_context>` — zero maintenance | free | any new extension using only the event bus |
| **platform delta** | Fork-only additive primitives: hooks/filters layer, `splitSystemPromptForCache`, `systemPrompt:build` filter, agent subsystem, OTEL | carries rebase surface; upstream-PR generics to shrink it | `getExtensionConfig` accessor (WS-B), new hooks added for WS-A |
| **behavior delta** | Inline patch to core behavior, not via hook/filter | forbidden; log in patch-inventory if unavoidable | — |

Rule: route new customization through the platform layer. Upstream-PR each generic platform-delta primitive once it matures in the fork.

## 4-layer config model

| Layer | What it is | Mechanism | Precedence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1 Capability** | Extension source code — built-in defaults | compiled constants / fallback values | lowest |
| **L2 Membership** | Profile manifest selects which extensions load | `pi.extensions[]` in profile `package.json` | ↑ |
| **L3 Tuning** | `settings.json extensionConfig{}` — per-extension key/value, deep-merged global ← project | `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor (WS-B) | ↑ |
| **L4 Override** | Env var / `--flag` for ephemeral or CI-level overrides | `registerFlag/getFlag`; env var fallback in accessor | highest |

`deepMergeSettings` already handles L3 today (unknown keys survive JSON.parse). The only missing piece is the `getExtensionConfig` accessor on `ExtensionAPI` (~15 LOC).

## Working process

- Delete finished workstreams as they land. DONE items get a commit hash + date inline; remove from active list once trimmed.
- Run the full gate before declaring any WS done: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` per shipped tranche (fork CHANGELOG for core changes; extension/package CHANGELOG for extension work).

---

## WS-B — Config layering (proof-of-concept, do first)

**Goal:** add `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` to `ExtensionAPI`, introduce `extensionConfig{}` in `settings.json`, and migrate `cache-base-prompt` off the `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT` env var to L3/L4.

### Steps

1. **`pi-mono-fork`: add `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor** (~15 LOC). Interface change in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts`; implementation on the `api` object built by `createExtensionAPI` in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` (`loader.ts:254`). Returns `mergedSettings.extensionConfig?.[namespace] ?? {}`. **Caveat (verified):** `createExtensionAPI(extension, runtime, cwd, eventBus)` has no settings handle today — step 1 must also thread the merged `Settings` (or a `() => Settings` getter) into the factory. There is no existing `getSettings()` to call. Shape: upstream-shapeable platform-delta primitive.
2. **`pi-mono-fork`: expose on `ExtensionHooksAPI`** so extensions can call `pi.getExtensionConfig("my-ext")`.
3. **`my-pi`: update `extensions/cache-base-prompt/index.ts`** — read `pi.getExtensionConfig("cache-base-prompt").extendBase` (boolean); fall back to `process.env.PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT === "1"` (L4 env override preserved).
4. **`my-pi`: update global/project `settings.json` examples** — document `extensionConfig: { "cache-base-prompt": { "extendBase": true } }`.
5. **Write/update docs** — `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` (new file, describes the 4-layer model + usage pattern).

### Acceptance criteria

- `pi.getExtensionConfig("cache-base-prompt")` returns the merged object from global and project `settings.json`.
- Removing `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT` from `~/.zshenv` and setting `extensionConfig` in `settings.json` produces identical runtime behavior.

# Config Layering

read_when: adding a new extension setting; migrating an env-var feature flag to settings.json; implementing getExtensionConfig; understanding why a setting override isn't taking effect; designing a new extension that needs per-project tuning.

---

## The L1-L4 model (precedence low → high)

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Who sets it | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | Extension source code (hardcoded defaults) | Extension author | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | Profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | `my-pi/packages/my-pi-*/package.json` | Including/excluding an extension from a profile |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}` block, deep-merged global ← project | Operator / Luke per-runtime or per-project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | Env var or CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | Shell environment, launch agent, CI secret | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

Higher layer wins. L4 always beats L3. L3 project settings beat L3 global settings (deep-merged, project keys win on conflict).

---

## Why this order

- **L1** is the extension's own defaults — it works with zero config.
- **L2** controls whether the extension loads at all. A miscategorized extension in the wrong profile is an L2 error.
- **L3** is the operator contract: `settings.json` is the stable, committed, reviewable place to tune behavior across runtimes. It survives restarts and is diffable.
- **L4** is the escape hatch: env vars and flags can override L3 without editing files — useful for CI secrets, one-off dev runs, emergency flips. They are not committed.

---

## extensionConfig{} in settings.json

Any `settings.json` (global at `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or project-local) may contain an `extensionConfig` key. The value is a plain object keyed by extension name (matching the extension's directory / package name). Values are arbitrary — whatever shape the extension expects.

```json
{
  "extensionConfig": {
    "cache-base-prompt": {
      "extendBase": true
    },
    "dream-memory": {
      "intervalMinutes": 30,
      "maxStoredItems": 200
    },
    "pi-memory": {
      "maxTurns": 5
    }
  }
}
```

Deep-merge behavior (from `deepMergeSettings` in `settings-manager.ts`): the global settings are the base; project settings are merged on top. For nested objects like `extensionConfig`, keys from the project object win at the leaf level — arrays are replaced, not concatenated.

This already works today. The settings JSON parser does NOT strip unknown keys (verified at `settings-manager.ts:334/408`), so `extensionConfig` blobs survive the parse and reach extensions unchanged.

---

## getExtensionConfig accessor (missing piece, ~15 LOC)

The only missing piece is a typed accessor on `ExtensionAPI` so extensions can read their config slice without reaching into the raw settings object.

Proposed signature (upstream-shaped, generic, ~15 LOC):

```typescript
// Method on the `api` object built by createExtensionAPI (loader.ts:254).
// NOTE: there is no settings handle in createExtensionAPI today — see caveat below.
getExtensionConfig<T = unknown>(namespace: string): T | undefined {
  return mergedSettings.extensionConfig?.[namespace] as T | undefined;
}
```

**Implementation caveat (verified):** `createExtensionAPI(extension, runtime, cwd, eventBus)` (`loader.ts:254`) does NOT receive the merged `Settings`, and neither it nor `ExtensionRuntime` exposes a `getSettings()`. So WS-B step 1 must first thread the merged settings (or a `() => Settings` getter) into the factory before the accessor can read anything. Do not assume an existing accessor.

Usage in an extension:

```typescript
pi.on("init", (pi) => {
  const cfg = pi.getExtensionConfig<{ extendBase?: boolean }>("cache-base-prompt");
  const extendBase = cfg?.extendBase ?? false;
  // ...
});
```

This is **upstreamable** — it is a generic, vendor-neutral accessor on the existing settings merge path. The `extensionConfig` key is just a convention namespace; upstream doesn't need to know what any extension puts in it.

Target: interface in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts`; implementation on the `api` object in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts` (`createExtensionAPI`, `loader.ts:254`). Track in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed.

---

## Migration example: cache-base-prompt

**Current state (L4 only):**

```
# ~/.zshenv
export PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1
```

Extension reads:
```typescript
const extendBase = process.env.PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT === "1";
```

This works on the laptop where `~/.zshenv` is sourced. It is invisible on pod/harness runtimes that don't source that file.

**Target state (L3 primary, L4 override):**

1. Add to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (global, applies to all runtimes):
```json
{
  "extensionConfig": {
    "cache-base-prompt": { "extendBase": true }
  }
}
```

2. Update extension to read L3 first, fall back to L4:
```typescript
pi.on("init", (pi) => {
  const cfg = pi.getExtensionConfig<{ extendBase?: boolean }>("cache-base-prompt");
  const extendBase = cfg?.extendBase ?? (process.env.PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT === "1");
  // ...
});
```

3. Keep `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT` as L4 override — it still works, it just no longer needs to be set everywhere. Remove it from `~/.zshenv` once all runtimes have the `settings.json` entry.

This is the proof-of-concept for the whole model. Once `getExtensionConfig` lands, migrate other env-var flags the same way.

---

## Per-runtime settings.json locations

| Runtime | settings.json path |
|---|---|
| Laptop (full) | `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (global) + `<project>/.pi/settings.json` (project) |
| openclaw (harness) | agentDir configured in the harness launch — check `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| k8s pods (pod) | Mounted as a ConfigMap or baked into the image; see pod deployment manifest |
| Action runners / clawsweeper | Set via env or a mounted config file per the clawsweeper deployment |

Project-level settings override global for that project directory only. If you need a setting everywhere, put it in the global file.

---

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't read `process.env.*` directly in new extension code** without an L3 fallback. Env vars are invisible to other runtimes and not diffable.
- **Don't add top-level keys to `Settings`** for extension-specific config. Use `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` — it keeps the namespace clean and avoids upstream schema conflicts.
- **Don't rely on L2 (profile membership) to carry behavior defaults** — that conflates "does this extension load" with "how is it tuned". Load via L2, tune via L3.

---

## Related docs

- `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — cache + system-prompt stability (read before touching extensionConfig keys that affect prompt construction)
- `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` — extension authoring conventions
- `my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — versioned registry seam (how L3 settings reach each runtime at deploy time)
- `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — track `getExtensionConfig` as a fork-first patch until upstreamed

## Anti-patterns

- **Don't read `process.env.*` directly in new extension code** without an L3 fallback. Env vars are invisible to other runtimes and not diffable.

- **Don't rely on L2 (profile membership) to carry behavior defaults** — that conflates "does this extension load" with "how is it tuned". Load via L2, tune via L3.
